name: Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA)
description: Finds the deepest node that is an ancestor of both given nodes. Classic recursive solution checks if target nodes are in left/right subtrees.
aim: Find the LCA of two nodes p and q: the deepest node that has both p and q as descendants (a node is a descendant of itself).
howItWorks: If root is null or equals p or q: return root
If both sides return non-null: current node is LCA
If only one side returns: propagate that result up

realWorld: Version control: find common ancestor of two commits
Taxonomy: closest common ancestor in classification tree
whenToUse: Finding relationship between two nodes in any tree
Graph problems reducible to tree LCA
alternatives: Binary lifting — O(log n) per query after O(n log n) preprocessing
Euler tour + RMQ — O(1) per query after O(n) preprocessing
